problem:
Let ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ be the solutions of the equation ${x}^{2}-10x=-21.$ Find the value ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}.$ 

*Hint: Use the fact that ${x}^{2}-10x+25$ is a perfect square.*

feedback.problem:
Let ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ be the solutions of the equation ${x}^{2}-6x=16.$ Find the value ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}.$ 

*Hint: Use the fact that ${x}^{2}-6x+9$ is a perfect square.*
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the hint, we have

$$
{x}^{2}-6x+9=(x-3{)}^{2}.
$$

First, we complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-6x & =16 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 3\cdot x & =16 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 3\cdot x+{3}^{2}-{3}^{2} & =16 \\ (x-3{)}^{2}-9 & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we isolate the perfect square by adding $9$ to both sides: 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3{)}^{2}-9+9 & =16+9 \\ (x-3{)}^{2} & =25\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve the equation using the square root method:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3{)}^{2} & =25 \\ \sqrt{(x-3{)}^{2}} & =\sqrt{25} \\ |x-3| & =5 \\ x-3 & =\pm 5 \\ x & =3\pm 5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify the two solutions:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =3-5=-2 \\ {x}_{2} & =3+5=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=(-2{)}^{2}+{8}^{2}=68.
$$
